page: Vultr vc2-24c-96gb is a high-capacity general-purpose cloud instance within the Cloud Compute lineup. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, the instance provisions 24 shared vCPUs across 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is balanced at a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, delivering 96.0 GB of system RAM (4.0 GB per vCPU). Hardware acceleration is absent, with no GPU integrated into the deployment.

Storage configuration includes a bundled 1600 GB local NVMe SSD, providing direct high-throughput disk access without requiring external volume attachments. In synthetic evaluation, the instance demonstrates mid-tier multi-threaded computational capabilities, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 29089.76, a stress-ng multi-core result of 32078.94, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7313.0. In-memory and caching operations remain consistent, recording 31.68 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a static web serving throughput of 15.77 GB/sec.

A clear performance tradeoff exists in single-threaded operations due to the conservative 2.0 GHz base clock speed and shared CPU architecture. This is reflected in lower single-core benchmark brackets, including a Geekbench single-core score of 838.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 23.37 GB/sec. Consequently, the instance is cost-efficient for parallelized workloads that benefit from large memory density and bundled high-capacity NVMe storage, but it is less suited for latency-sensitive or strictly single-threaded execution.

Primary workload fits include distributed relational databases, Redis caching clusters, CI/CD build servers, batch data processing, containerized microservices, and general-purpose enterprise application hosting.
